name: Joachim Lange
credit: No portrait available (monogram tile). Text: G. Osborn (ed.), The Poetical Works of John and Charles Wesley, 13 vols (London: Wesleyan-Methodist Conference Office, 1868–72), from Internet Archive scans (OCR).
bio: Joachim Lange (1670–1744) was a pietist theologian at Halle and a hymn-writer; his “O Jesu, süßes Licht” appears in the Herrnhuth Collection (No. 308) and in Knapp’s Evangelischer Liederschatz.
The single piece here is John Wesley’s English translation, printed in Hymns and Sacred Poems (1739); Osborn’s footnote names Joachim Lange as the author of the German original.

poems.title: A Morning Dedication of Ourselves to Christ
poems.author: Joachim Lange
poems.collection: Hymns and Sacred Poems (1739) · Osborn ed., vol. 1 (1868); German: O Jesu, süßes Licht
poems.note: Translated from the German by John Wesley; Osborn's note names the original author and the German hymn “O Jesu, süßes Licht”.
poems.text:
Jesu, Thy light again I view,
Again Thy mercy's beams I see,
And all within me wakes, anew
To pant for Thy immensity:
Again my thoughts to Thee aspire
In fervent flames of strong desire.

But, O! what offering shall I give
To Thee, the Lord of earth and skies?
My spirit, soul, and flesh receive
A holy, living sacrifice.
Small as it is, 'tis all my store:
More shouldst Thou have, if I had more.

Now then, my God, Thou hast my soul;
No longer mine, but Thine I am:
Guard Thou Thy own; possess it whole,
Cheer it by hope, with love inflame.
Thou hast my spirit; there display
Thy glory to the perfect day.

Thou hast my flesh; Thy hallow'd shrine,
Devoted solely to Thy will:
Here let Thy light for ever shine,
This house still let Thy presence fill:
O Source of Life, live, dwell, and move
In me, till all my life be love.

O, never in -these veils of shame,
Sad fruits of sin, my glorying be!
Clothe with salvation through Thy name
My soul, and may I put on Thee!
Be living faith my costly dress,
And my best robe Thy righteousness!

Send down Thy likeness from above,
And let this my adorning be:
Clothe me with wisdom, patience, love,
With lowhness and purity,
Than gold and pearls more precious far,
And brighter than the morning star.

Lord, arm me with Thy Spirit's might,
Since I am call'd by Thy great name:
In Thee my wandering thoughts unite,
Of all my works be Thou the aim.
Thy love attend me all my days,
And my sole business be Thy praise!
